summary: This work presents the first in-situ magic state injection scheme for arbitrary CSS qLDPC codes, where logical magic states are prepared directly within a code block using only syndrome extraction resources. Circuit-level simulations on the $[[144,12,12]]$ Bivariate Bicycle code achieve injection error rates of $1.62 \times 10^{-3}$ per logical qubit when simultaneously injecting four logical $|Y\rangle$ states under depolarizing noise at $p=10^{-3}$, falling to $6.7 \times 10^{-4}$ under asymmetric noise where single-qubit errors are 10% of two-qubit errors.
motivation: Existing magic state injection proposals for qLDPC codes rely on external prepare-and-transfer paradigms that require separate auxiliary blocks, whereas qLDPC codes naturally encode multiple logical qubits in a single block at low overhead. A native in-situ injection primitive is needed to leverage this advantage for non-Clifford resource state preparation.
method: The scheme identifies carrier qubits and peeled qubits via stabilizer cleaning, then resolves overlaps in logical $X$ and $Z$ supports through Bell state preparation on compatible pairings. A noise-aware variant optimizes initial state configurations to maximize first-round protection of injected logical supports using mixed-integer linear programming, enabling post-selection on fixed stabilizers with deterministic measurement outcomes.
result: For the $[[144,12,12]]$ BB code injecting four logical qubits: injection error rate $1.62 \times 10^{-3}$ per logical qubit (uniform depolarizing, $p=10^{-3}$); $6.7 \times 10^{-4}$ per logical qubit (asymmetric noise with $p_{1Q}=0.1p_{2Q}$); discard rate 93%; correlated errors contribute only $\sim 1\%$ of total error. The $[[225,9,4]]$ hypergraph product code achieves $8 \times 10^{-3}$ per logical qubit when injecting six logicals, demonstrating generality across CSS qLDPC families.
